The response-only barrier is the smallest discriminator for whether support publication retains the earlier persistence dependency.

obligation.description: With asynchronous storage writes, a positive append acknowledgment for log state whose local append remains incomplete must not be exposed as an immediately deliverable message. Its publication must remain behind ordered append work whose completion establishes the acknowledged state, including when the acknowledgment is generated by a duplicate accepted append and the current Ready contains no new entries.

scope.description: Library-to-caller message publication dependency for positive remote MsgAppResp under the asynchronous storage interface, with a legal accepted append followed by a duplicate before local storage completion.
assumptions: Message duplication is exact and originates from an actual leader-produced MsgApp in the same execution.
The caller processes local append messages reliably and in order and releases attached responses only after completion.
No crash, membership change or malformed network message is needed.
excluded: Disk crash persistence, global agreement after restart and client-visible application results.
Liveness under indefinite local storage delay.

grounding.derivation: s-async-config-contract requires durable completion before delivering append response messages and reliable ordering of append work. s-ready-contract says async top-level messages may be sent immediately, while completion-dependent messages are attached to storage messages. Thus an acknowledgment relying on pending entries must retain a storage dependency even when that Ready has no new entries. s-send identifies append replies as durability-dependent support. The requirement follows these interface responsibilities, not an assertion that every received append must succeed.
grounding.applicability: Select AsyncStorageWrites on the public RawNode interface. Delay actual local append work finitely while redelivering a produced append. Inspect top-level versus attached output, then finish work in order. Any MemoryStorage update is a deterministic storage-completion stand-in; it does not measure physical disk durability.

alternatives: The synchronous package guide and Ready interface disagree on same-batch entry/message concurrency; neither is used to authorize this asynchronous schedule.
An implementation could use a different barrier representation if it still prevents immediate delivery before completion; the essential property is the publication dependency.
